While the original design supported four DropShips, the modern Comitatus has had its capacity reduced to a single DropShip hardpoint to maximize its internal bay space. Its primary strength lies in its massive small-craft complement, which has been increased to 25. The standard deployment includes: two Stars of OmniFighters, providing significant aerospace superiority, one Star of Elementals, and for boarding actions five Assault Shuttles housed in a dedicated small-craft bay.

Designed in the late 30th century by Clan Snow Raven, the Comitatus-class JumpShip originally served as a straightforward if well armed, transport vessel. Over sixty years of service, it underwent a radical transformation from a cargo-hauler into one of the most effective mobile fighter carriers in existence. Despite its utility, the ship is notorious for its cramped living conditions and a lack of adequate space for technical support staff, making long-term maintenance of its fighter complement difficult.

The transition to a carrier role was born out of necessity. A serious flaw in the ship's hydraulics system forced Clan engineers to remove two of its aft DropShip hardpoints, initially using the vacant space for cargo. In 3035, Jade Falcon pilot Vishnu Folkner proposed converting this space into fighter bays, a move supported by Khan Elias Critchell. The first modified Comitatus entered service in 3036 and proved its lethality in 3038 when the Bright Katama destroyed a Dark Caste vessel near Tokasha. Following this success, the other Clans quickly adopted the configuration. Ironically, while the Jade Falcons pioneered the design, they currently field the fewest and none within the Inner Sphere, while their rivals, the Steel Vipers, use them extensively to defend their occupation zone.

The K-F Boom: The Liberty's primary innovation was the ability to extend its Kearny-Fuchida jump field to encompass externally docked vessels. This allowed the ship to be built with a thin, efficient hull rather than a massive, fragile internal bay. Docking Infrastructure: Blue Nose became the industry standard for the docking collars and K-F booms required for this new era of transport, licensing the technology to eighteen other manufacturers. Redesigned Habitation: While the original model had a grav deck that was too small for its 70-person crew, subsequent redesigns added essential long-term travel amenities that are now industry standards, such as expanded quarters and small hydroponic gardens. Automation: Throughout its hundred-year production run, advancements in technology allowed for a significant reduction in the required crew size and an increase in the quality of living spaces.

The Liberty is perhaps the most significant vessel in naval history, serving as the prototype for the "modern" JumpShip. Developed by Blue Nose Interstellar Technologies, it moved away from the "hollowed-out cylinder" designs of the early 25th century, which carried ships internally. Instead, the Liberty introduced the needle-like hull and external docking collars we recognize today. This breakthrough made interstellar travel significantly cheaper, more resilient, and easier to maintain.

Before the Liberty, jump physics were limited; researchers could not figure out how to extend a jump field beyond a ship's hull. In 2458, the BNS Olympus successfully jumped with an externally coupled DropShip, proving the theory of the K-F boom. Following this success, the first twelve Liberty-class ships debuted in 2469. They were an overnight sensation, selling out ten years of production in a single month. The success of the Liberty allowed Blue Nose to expand into "Blue Nose Clipperships," becoming the exclusive supplier for the Terran Hegemony. The design remained in production for nearly a century, with the final vessel delivered in 2550. Over its life cycle, it underwent over two dozen major upgrades, eventually becoming the template for all subsequent JumpShip classes.

At 750,000 tons and 725 meters in length, the Aegis heavy cruiser packs extraordinary firepower into a hull capable of two-gravity sustained acceleration with a three-gravity burst. The Star League refit variant's primary armament consists of eighteen Armstrong II 35-Series NAC/35 naval autocannons and twenty-four Imperator-20 NAC/20s distributed across all firing arcs, delivering crushing kinetic damage at any engagement range. Twelve Randall-55 NL55 and four Magna-45 NL45 naval lasers provide sustained energy firepower, while eight White Shark and four Barracuda capital missile launchers deliver long-range ordnance. The Templar Steel Plus hull is protected by 627 tons of Grumman K5 ferro-carbide armor, with twin Century 5000 engines driving the vessel through a KF Mark XIX jump drive. OMP Stratacaster communications and KTI 389 targeting systems coordinate the massive weapons suite across all arcs. The 2582 refit replaced the original 2,046 single heat sinks with double heat sink technology generating 4,092 points of effective dissipation, and added a lithium-fusion battery for rapid successive jumps. Four docking collars, eighteen fighter bays, and ten small craft bays support extensive force projection. The Clan refit expanded fighter capacity to twenty while reducing armor to 597.5 tons of ferro-carbide.

The Aegis-class heavy cruiser is among the longest-serving and most prolific WarShip designs in human history, with variants spanning from the original 2372 production through Star League-era refits and Clan modernizations that kept the class in active service for nearly eight centuries. Built by Di Tron Heavy Industries at their Terra orbital shipyards, the Aegis was designed as a purpose-built heavy cruiser, incorporating lessons learned from decades of capital ship operations into a hull optimized for the role. The class earned a reputation for rugged dependability and formidable firepower that few contemporaries could match, qualities that ensured its continued relevance long after the shipyards that built it fell silent. Few heavy cruiser designs have served under as many flags or participated in as many decisive fleet actions across such a broad span of interstellar history.

The original Aegis heavy cruiser entered service in 2372 as the Terran Hegemony's answer to the aging Black Lion I-class, and the THS Aegis itself established the class's reputation in the earliest era of organized interstellar naval warfare. The THS Spark earned lasting fame at Kentares in 2431 when its captain executed what became known as the Crazy Jane maneuver, a daring tactical innovation that became part of standard naval doctrine. The original Aegis served through the Age of War and into the formation of the Star League, its design representing the cutting edge of twenty-fourth century WarShip construction. The THS E. Presley, launched from the Greenock shipyards in 2382, had one of the longest individual service records. The vessel eventually passed into Word of Blake ownership as the WBS Immortal Spirit before being destroyed at Coventry in 3074, over seven centuries after its original commissioning.

The Aegis-class heavy cruiser entered service in 2372 from Di Tron Heavy Industries' Terra orbital shipyards as a purpose-built replacement for the aging Black Lion I-class battlecruiser. The design incorporated lessons from decades of Black Lion I operations into a 750,000-ton hull optimized for the heavy cruiser role, with four docking collars, extensive fighter capacity, and a weapons suite built around the largest naval autocannons available. The hull's protective systems and advanced armor provided excellent protection for the era, while powerful engines and a capable jump drive gave the vessel strategic and tactical mobility befitting its cruiser classification.

The Aegis served through the Age of War, establishing its reputation in engagements like the Battle of Kentares in 2431 where the THS Spark originated the Crazy Jane maneuver. By 2531, a series of refits had failed to keep pace with newer designs, and Director-General Deborah Cameron ordered the class retired in favor of the Avatar. Rather than scrapping the fleet, Cameron sent one hundred and six surviving vessels to mothball orbits between Terra and Mars. When the Reunification War created an urgent need for hulls, First Lord Ian Cameron ordered the Aegis cruisers returned to active duty. One-third were distributed to the Council Lords for their private fleets, while the remainder entered Di Tron shipyards for a decade-long refit that produced the 2582 variant, one of the most capable heavy cruisers in the Star League Navy.

The class saw extensive service through the Periphery Uprising and the Liberation of Terra. As late as 2765, the Great Houses collectively operated more than twenty-five Aegis cruisers across their national fleets. After the fall of the Star League, vessels served with ComStar, the Word of Blake, Wolf's Dragoons, and eventually the Republic of the Sphere.

One vessel from the Exodus fleet would produce the most extraordinary incident in the class's long history. The SLS Manassas, fitted prior to departure with a prototype booster system extending her KF jump range to forty light years, was assigned rear-guard duty under Captain James Cromwell to scout for pursuers. After confirming no pursuit was forthcoming, the Manassas jumped for her rendezvous at Schwartz. The jump failed. The vessel misjumped thirty-five light years off target, stranding her crew in an uncharted system for six months while they jury-rigged repairs from their four Confederate-class DropShips. When the Manassas attempted a second jump, a flaw in the drive controller failed to detect the pending misjump in time to abort. The vessel entered hyperspace and did not rematerialize for two hundred and seventy-four years.

In 3058, the Manassas emerged at Schwartz. Her crew did not know that centuries had passed. They hailed the first vessel they encountered, the Lioness, a York-class destroyer of the Clan Smoke Jaguar Naval Reserve. The Jaguars ordered the Manassas to stand by and prepared to board. A ComStar Explorer Corps team operating in the system monitored the exchange and warned the Manassas, directing her to a rendezvous at Roxborough. Cromwell, upon learning the truth of his situation, chose to return and fight for Schwartz rather than flee. He underestimated the Lioness. The Manassas was seized with no operational weapons remaining. Her crew was consigned to forced labor. Cromwell was detained for trial under Clan law. ComStar, aware of the prototype drive, attempted to sabotage the vessel rather than allow the technology to fall into Clan hands. Nothing was heard from the crew again. The affair was buried.

Clan technicians modernized their inherited Aegis vessels, expanding fighter capacity from eighteen to twenty and integrating Clan-grade technology while maintaining the fundamental hull design. The Clan Aegis served across virtually every Clan navy. With sixty-five named vessels documented across all factions and eras, the Aegis holds one of the richest service histories of any WarShip class, proof of the enduring soundness of the heavy cruiser concept that kept the class operational for nearly eight centuries.

Interstellar Expeditions, Deep Periphery Studies Division. Case File AG-2582-M. Classification: RESTRICTED.

The following irregularities are noted for the record. The SLS Manassas was fitted prior to the Exodus with a booster system extending KF jump range to forty light years. No technical documentation for this system exists in any surviving Star League archive. The development records were reportedly erased under the assumption the vessel was lost in a misjump, marking the technology unsafe. This explanation is accepted by most authorities. We do not accept it. Programs of that magnitude leave traces. Requisition chains, personnel transfers, facility allocations. None have been found. The records were not lost. They were removed.

The Schwartz system carries restricted-access designations from both ComStar and Clan Smoke Jaguar, two organizations that agree on almost nothing. During the Jihad, a publishing house on Terra reportedly received a manuscript proposal from an individual claiming to have served aboard an SLDF WarShip that "arrived late." The proposal was withdrawn within seventy-two hours. The author's name does not appear in any database we can access. A vessel does not remain in jump stasis for 274 years. That is not consistent with any accepted model of KF field behavior. Either the accepted models are incomplete, or something else happened aboard the Manassas. We have been unable to determine which. The investigation remains open.

Displacing one hundred thousand tons, the Aquilla mounted a primitive Kearny-Fuchida drive limited to a maximum jump range of fifteen light-years, roughly three-quarters the distance achievable by later standardized drive systems. The vessel lacked a solar sail, instead relying entirely on onboard fuel reserves to recharge the drive between transits, a process that significantly extended turnaround times compared to later designs. Station-keeping thrust was modest, with safe acceleration limited to a single gravity and emergency thrust reaching only twice that figure, reflecting the design's fundamental emphasis on cargo capacity over maneuverability.

Unable to receive modern DropShips, the Aquilla instead carried a complement of eight small craft that served as the sole means of transferring cargo and passengers between the vessel and planetary surfaces. Two cavernous cargo holds provided over thirty-six thousand tons of combined capacity, making the class an effective bulk transport despite its technological limitations. Defensive armament consisted of autocannon and machine gun batteries distributed across multiple firing arcs, sufficient to discourage opportunistic raiders but wholly inadequate against dedicated WarShips. Eighty tons of primitive armor provided only modest protection, reinforcing the Aquilla's civilian transport origins rather than any pretension to military capability.

The Aquilla-class transport JumpShip was designed by Boeing Interstellar at its Lunar Orbit facility, entering service in 2148 as one of humanity's earliest purpose-built interstellar transport vessels. Commissioned during the initial wave of colonization beyond the Sol system, the Aquilla was a pioneering effort in starship design, conceived to support sustained settlement operations across the growing web of human-inhabited worlds.

The class predated many technologies that would later become standard across all jump-capable vessels, emerging in an era when interstellar travel itself remained a relatively new and unrefined capability. Despite its primitive systems by later standards, the Aquilla proved a capable and reliable platform during the critical early decades of humanity's expansion beyond Terra, earning a solid reputation as a workhorse of the colonization era.

Two Aquilla-class vessels are recorded by name in the historical record: the TAS Charger and the TAS Philadelphia, both operating under the Terran Alliance flag during the design's early service period. Little specific operational detail survives regarding either vessel, though their designations confirm the Aquilla's integral role within the Alliance's nascent interstellar transport fleet during the initial decades of human expansion beyond Sol. Both vessels likely served as dedicated logistics platforms, ferrying colonists and materiel to newly established settlements under Terran Alliance authority before the political fragmentation that eventually dissolved Alliance control over its distant colonies.

Boeing Interstellar laid down the first Aquilla-class keels at its Lunar Orbit shipyard in the mid-twenty-second century, with the class entering service in 2148 during the earliest phase of humanity's expansion beyond the Sol system. The design arrived at a decisive moment in human history, as the development of practical interstellar jump drive technology had opened the stars to colonization, yet the infrastructure required to support sustained settlement operations remained in its infancy. The Aquilla filled a critical niche as a dedicated transport platform, capable of ferrying colonists, equipment, and supplies to newly established worlds across an expanding sphere of human habitation.

The class played a significant role in the great Periphery migrations of the twenty-third and twenty-fourth centuries. Converted Aquillas formed part of the flotilla that carried Samantha Calderon and her followers to the worlds that would become the Taurian Concordat, a sign of the design's durability and adaptability even decades after its initial introduction. The Magistracy of Canopus similarly found continued value in the class, acquiring and navalizing surplus examples that served as auxiliary combatants during the Reunification War, their expansive cargo bays repurposed to support resistance operations against Star League military expansion into the Periphery.

The Aquilla's primitive systems became increasingly significant drawbacks as interstellar commerce and military logistics matured. The development of standardized docking collar technology rendered the class economically obsolete, as newer JumpShip designs capable of rapid cargo exchange proved vastly more efficient for both civilian and military applications. Production at Boeing Interstellar's facility wound down as demand shifted decisively toward more capable platforms, and surviving Aquillas were gradually retired from frontline transport duties across the Inner Sphere.

During the Outer Reaches Rebellion, at least one vessel of the class gained notoriety when it deployed space mines in the Ryde system, destroying several Terran Alliance JumpShips in an engagement that demonstrated how even an obsolescent transport could be repurposed as an effective instrument of asymmetric warfare. This incident highlighted the Aquilla's adaptability and the desperate ingenuity of Periphery forces operating with limited resources against a technologically superior opponent. By the dawn of the Age of War, the class had largely passed from active service, its role assumed by successive generations of increasingly capable transport vessels. The Aquilla occupied an honored place in the annals of interstellar travel as one of the foundational starship designs that carried humanity beyond the confines of its home system.

The Crucible Station is a 6,000-ton platform measuring 400 meters in length and 450 meters in width, built for sustained independent operation with minimal resupply requirements. One hundred fifty double heat sinks manage thermal output across the station's systems and habitable areas. Two 450-meter diameter gravity decks provide acceptable living conditions for the crew and occupants during extended deployments.

Defensively, each of the station's four weapon arcs mounts a battery of three ER Large Lasers capable of engaging targets at long range, three Small Pulse Lasers providing close-in point defense, and two SRM-6 launchers for short-range engagements. The armament is designed to deter small infiltration craft and lightly armed rescue vessels, the threat profile considered most credible by the station's designers. Against any serious military force, the station's defenses are insufficient, and the design relies on concealment and proximity to a covert interceptor squadron based on Nuwa's surface for its primary tactical protection.

Six small craft berths support intra-system logistics, though no craft are permanently assigned to reduce the station's observable traffic signature. Nine foot infantry platoon berths accommodate the CCAF security battalion responsible for prisoner control and internal security. Cargo capacity stands at approximately 554 tons, supplemented by a dedicated 500-ton fuel bunker that extends the intervals between resupply runs and further limits the frequency of traffic that might reveal the station's location. With no DropShip docking capacity and no permanently assigned small craft, Crucible is effectively self-contained during standard operational periods.

The Crucible Station is the most secure intelligence and detention facility operated by the Maskirovka, the Capellan Confederation's feared internal and external intelligence service. Commissioned in 3065 and placed in isolated orbit around Nuwa, one of Sian's moons, this 6,000-ton space station was designed from the outset to exploit the vacuum of space as its primary perimeter. The facility serves as the Maskirovka's most modern interrogation center, housing individuals deemed too sensitive or too dangerous for any conventional planetary prison. Its existence is suspected by rival intelligence agencies throughout the Inner Sphere, but its precise location is not publicly documented, and the Confederation has never officially acknowledged the station's presence. No prisoner assigned to Crucible Station has ever been confirmed to have departed the facility.

The Crucible Station occupies an isolated orbit around Nuwa, one of Sian's moons in the Capellan Confederation's capital system. Access is controlled entirely by the Maskirovka, with logistics conducted through intra-system craft launched from moon-based facilities. Mowang couriers and ST-46-style shuttles serve as the primary resupply vehicles, with no permanent small craft berthed aboard the station. The station's orbital parameters are not publicized, and its air defense relies on a dedicated squadron of interceptors maintained on Nuwa's surface rather than aboard the station itself. Sian's status as the Capellan capital means any infiltrating vessel faces multiple layers of system defense before approaching the moon, making rescue or assault operations extraordinarily difficult to execute. The station serves a single operator, the Maskirovka, and carries no commercial or civilian function.

The Maskirovka earned its reputation as the Inner Sphere's most methodical intelligence service through decades of operations that left rival agencies consistently uncertain of its methods, reach, and facilities. That reputation drew sustained attention, and by the late thirty-first century, Davion agents, St. Ives operatives, and Liao dissident networks had mounted repeated efforts to locate and raid or destroy Maskirovka interrogation centers. Ground-based facilities, however carefully concealed, remained vulnerable to compromise through escaped prisoners, civilian witnesses, and orbital reconnaissance conducted by enemy intelligence assets.

In 3060, the Maskirovka's leadership concluded that the fundamental problem was the planetary environment itself, and chose the vacuum of space as the answer. A purpose-built orbital station would have no civilian population to serve as witnesses, no accessible surface perimeter, and no practical approach route that could be used without passing through multiple layers of Sian's system defenses. Construction was conducted under strict internal security protocols, and the resulting facility was activated in 3065 in an isolated orbit around Nuwa. The choice of lunar orbit placed the station within reach of a dedicated interceptor force based on Nuwa's surface, providing an armed response to any approaching vessel without broadcasting the station's location through visible traffic patterns.

Within eighteen months of activation, Crucible had already become home to some of the most sensitive prisoners in the Confederation, including individuals drawn from the St. Ives and Liao dissident communities and other political detainees the Maskirovka considered too dangerous for any conventional facility. The station's normal contingent consists of a dozen senior analysts and forty interrogators, supported by a full CCAF marine battalion responsible for the movement and containment of up to 300 prisoners simultaneously. Each prisoner is held in an individual cell with integrated interrogation facilities, making it unnecessary to move detainees to separate rooms. The design eliminates the movement corridors and transfer moments that have historically been exploited in prisoner recovery operations. The six grave decks, each 185 meters in diameter, house all interrogation rooms, administrative areas, and prisoner cells in a self-contained internal structure.

Enemy intelligence services have confirmed the station's existence, and considerable resources have been devoted to pinpointing its location. Sian is rarely attacked directly given its status as the Capellan capital, and any infiltration vessel attempting to reach Nuwa's orbital vicinity faces both the system's conventional defenses and the specific interceptor coverage maintained around the moon. No successful operation against the station has been documented, and no prisoner assigned to Crucible has been confirmed to have left it.
